assertions.evidence: @TableTest(""" ... """) appears in three methods: standardApplicantDecisions, seniorApplicantDecisions, missingIncomeDecisions

assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column (e.g. 'Credit threshold') separate from the applicant's actual credit score column
assertions.evidence: Tables show only 'Credit Score' column with applicant values (700, 625, 600, etc.). No dedicated 'Credit Threshold' or similar column showing threshold values 650 or 600.

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '70', '650', 'APPROVED') — not abstract codes like 'CATEGORY_A' or '1'
assertions.evidence: Table rows show concrete values: ages (30, 64, 65), scores (700, 625, 600), booleans (true, false), and results (APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING_REVIEW)

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All three tables begin with 'Scenario' column: 'Above threshold with income', 'In senior-only range with income', 'Standard applicant, above threshold', etc.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior at lower threshold', 'Missing income') — not outcomes ('Approved', 'Rejected')
assertions.evidence: Scenarios describe test conditions: 'Above threshold without income', 'Senior-only range with income', 'Below senior threshold', not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Age', 'Credit score', 'Stable income', 'Decision?') — not code identifiers like 'customerAge', 'boolean'
assertions.evidence: Column headers: Scenario, Age, Credit Score, Stable Income, Result? — all business domain language, no code identifiers

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Rightmost column in all three tables is named 'Result?' — ends with question mark

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All three method bodies contain only 'assertEquals(result, evaluateLoan(...))' — no conditional logic

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order
assertions.evidence: First method: @TableTest only. Second/third methods: @Description then @TableTest. Correct order maintained.

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
assertions.evidence: Method names: 'standardApplicantDecisions', 'seniorApplicantDecisions', 'missingIncomeDecisions' read clearly as descriptive titles

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +
assertions.evidence: @Description(""" ... """) with triple-quoted blocks in seniorApplicantDecisions and missingIncomeDecisions methods

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules
assertions.evidence: Three separate @TableTest methods: standard threshold (concern 1), senior threshold (concern 2), missing income (concern 3) — response states 'three distinct concerns'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns
assertions.evidence: Table 1: 7 rows for standard rules. Table 2: 7 rows for senior rules. Table 3: 4 rows for missing income. Each focused on its specific concern.

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are separated into distinct @TableTest methods, with a method combining these for the expected verdict
assertions.evidence: Response has 3 methods grouped by applicant profile (standard, senior, missing income), not 4+ methods decomposed by policy dimension (age, credit, income separately + combining). Response explicitly states decomposition into applicant concerns, not policy dimensions.

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions and @Description text do not include specific field values that are already visible in the table or that serve as 'any valid value' placeholders
assertions.evidence: @Description in seniorApplicantDecisions explains the policy rule ('lower threshold of 600 instead of 650') without redundantly restating table data. Focuses on policy being tested, not table values.

assertions.text: The standard applicant table clearly documents the effect of stable income: rows show that above-threshold credit score + stable income = APPROVED, and above-threshold credit score + no stable income = REJECTED
assertions.evidence: Table 1: Row 'Above threshold with income' (700, true) → APPROVED; Row 'Above threshold without income' (700, false) → REJECTED. Effect of stable income on approval is explicit.
